Build a transport network

Source: R/network.R
build_network.Rd

Builds a multimodal transport network from a directory with one 'OpenStreetMap' extract (.pbf), zero or more 'GTFS' feeds (.zip) and, optionally, an elevation raster (.tif). The network lives in memory and is reused by every routing function; nothing is written to data_path. The files are recognised by their extension in lower case only: a map.PBF or a feed.ZIP is ignored.

Usage

build_network(
  data_path,
  verbose = FALSE,
  temp_dir = FALSE,
  elevation = "TOBLER",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  n_threads = Inf
)

Arguments

data_path

A string, the directory with the .pbf file, the 'GTFS' feeds and the elevation raster.

verbose

A logical. Whether to report the build of the network in messages. Defaults to FALSE.

temp_dir

A logical, checked but without effect: nothing is downloaded or cached.

elevation

A string, the slope cost function for walking and cycling when data_path has a .tif elevation raster: "TOBLER" (the default; Tobler's hiking function), "MINETTI" (Minetti's energy cost of walking) or "NONE" (no slope costs).

overwrite

A logical, checked but without effect: the network is always built anew.

n_threads

The number of threads used to read the .pbf file. Defaults to Inf, all cores (two under R CMD check when it limits the cores).

Value

A peabiru_network object to pass to the routing functions (printing it summarises the network).

Elevation

A .tif raster in data_path gives walking and cycling times slope costs (elevation = "TOBLER", the default, or "MINETTI"; never for cars): the raster is sampled every 10 m along each street at the nearest pixel, and each street's time is multiplied by the average cost of its slopes. Points outside the raster count as 0 m high. Without a .tif raster the network is built with elevation = "NONE".

The raster must be a GeoTIFF with one band, north up, uncompressed or compressed with LZW, Deflate or PackBits (what GDAL writes by default), in WGS 84 longitude and latitude (EPSG:4326) or another coordinate reference system given by its EPSG code (what GDAL writes) whose transform is reproduced exactly: SIRGAS 2000 (4674), SAD69 (4618), Corrego Alegre 1970-72 (4225), their UTM zones used in Brazil (31965-31985, 6210, 6211, 5396; 29168-29172, 29187-29195; 22521-22525), SIRGAS 2000 / Brazil Polyconic (5880), WGS 84 / UTM (32601-32660, 32701-32760) and WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator (3857). Other rasters are an error that says what to change, and so are a .prj file next to the raster, a raster whose name ends in .tiff and more than one raster.

Elevations are kept in decimetres in 16-bit integers: voids and values beyond +/-3276.7 m wrap around (SRTM's -32768 voids become 0 m, -9999 becomes 3108.2 m, a NaN no-data value 0 m), with a warning counting them and the samples equal to the raster's no-data value.

In a system other than EPSG:4326 the pixel read for a street point within nanometres (5e-8 m, or 2e-13 degrees) of the boundary between two pixels, or of the raster's edge, depends on the last bits of the sines and cosines of the projection. peabiru computes them itself, bit for bit the same way, so the result is the same on every machine, and warns once with the number of such points (about one in a hundred million for 30 m pixels; reprojecting the raster to EPSG:4326 removes the ambiguity). A point that falls on the raster's outer edge (inside its envelope, past the last pixel) is an error, since there is no pixel to read.

A raster also turns off the swap of origins and destinations of walking matrices (see travel_time_matrix()), and a routing call with a scenario (new_carspeeds, carspeed_scale, new_lts) runs without the slope costs, with a warning.

Public transport

The 'GTFS' feeds are loaded in the order in which the operating system lists the directory. With more than one feed that order depends on the file system, so the same directory can give slightly different expanded and arrival matrices on two machines (another stop or route for a few trips); on one machine the results are always the same.

The network is not built when a 'GTFS' feed has errors of priority "HIGH" (a reference to a stop, route, trip, service or agency that does not exist, a number that cannot be read, tables in a subfolder of the .zip, routes without any agency): the error names the feeds and points to get_gtfs_errors(), which lists the errors. A feed that cannot be loaded at all is an error too.

The network object

The network is held in memory by the 'Rust' engine and is always built anew: there is no cache on disk, and a network cannot be saved with saveRDS() or carried to another session (a reloaded one is refused with an error; build it again). More than one .pbf file in data_path is an error.

See also

Other network functions: check_transit_availability(), find_snap(), get_gtfs_errors(), street_network_bbox(), street_network_to_sf(), transit_network_to_sf()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
network
#> <peabiru_network>
#>   data path: /Users/leite/Github/peabiru-routing/.claude/scratch/sessao-1112/ns/rlib-015/peabiru/extdata/spo
#>   streets:   2,609 vertices, 5,518 edges
#>   transit:   1 feed(s) (spo_gtfs), 654 stops, 36 patterns, 6 services, frequency-based trips
#>   elevation: NONE
